answer: Isolated cluster congestion pricing throttles bandwidth when traffic density inside a local topological grove exceeds normal routing capacity. To bypass this enforcement rule, an attacker must flood adjacent nodes with high-volume garbage data to forge artificial connectivity. The resulting operational cost requires sustaining immense computational overhead across every karst routing path they attempt to manipulate. Ultimately, this structural friction turns any resource-draining fable of rapid network dominance into an economically unviable strategy.
